reviewer: Claude Code implementer self-review (the same agent session that wrote the change; not independent review)

reviewScope.summary: Self-review of a release-control change stacked on PR #97: the workflow runs Plan certification, a Unit stage and three E2E shards in parallel, and Final candidate verifies every stage of the same attempt and writes the single comprehensive manifest. The ATTEST verifier accepts only that exact job set, all successful, under contract version 2. Application code, tests other than release controls, and the local single-process gate are unchanged.
evidence: Owner instruction 2026-11-15: waiting is a serious bottleneck and extra Actions minutes are acceptable; split as far as defensible.
Two production builds of the same checkout were byte-identical (aggregate SHA-256 83e2604c...), so the assembler can require each shard to have tested exactly the build the unit stage checked.

scripts/release-stages.mjs assembleStages rejects, with tests: a missing shard, a failed stage, a stage from another run or attempt, a different commit, a different review, a shard that tested a different build, a skipped command, a shard run with another shard spec, a nonzero exit, a retried test and a changed test report (14 of 14 pass).

scripts/release-reuse.mjs requires exactly Plan certification, Unit stage, E2E shards 1/3 to 3/3 and Final candidate, all completed successfully in the source attempt; new cases reject a failed, missing, duplicated or other-attempt stage job. The reuse suite passes 62 of 62, and all release-script tests 140 of 140.

The single-job ATTEST shape is preserved where it matters: one Final candidate job and check, one artifact named release-evidence-final-candidate rooted at the repository, and one -pass-N manifest whose start and end lie inside the Final candidate job. Stage manifests use -stage- names, so they cannot be mistaken for it.

Run #204's upload log shows upload-artifact computes the artifact root from the listed search paths even when some are absent, so the Final candidate upload keeps its three paths and its repository-rooted entries.
Stage modules load lazily; the review-binding runner tests, which copy only the original three gate files, still pass, so a local full gate never depends on them.

tests/architecture/releaseWorkflow.test.ts pins the job graph: Final candidate needs plan, unit and e2e with if: always(), stage jobs are skipped only for ATTEST, Final candidate requires all three results to be success before assembling, and the ladder reads the E2E job ceiling. Architecture tests 158 of 158 pass.

Preflight: Prettier, ESLint with --max-warnings 0, npm run typecheck and git diff --check on the candidate. No hosted run of this workflow exists yet; the first PR run is the first execution of the staged graph.

adversarialFindings.description: Final candidate could pass on evidence that was not produced by this attempt, by a failed stage, or for another build.
adversarialFindings.resolution: The assembler binds every stage to GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT and the control fingerprint, requires passed status, the exact command profile, valid report digests and counts, zero skips and retries, and byte-identical build checksums. The workflow also requires all three needs results to be success.

adversarialFindings.description: ATTEST could reuse a PR run whose stage jobs did not all succeed.
adversarialFindings.resolution: discoverSource requires exactly the expected job names, each completed successfully with the same run, attempt and head SHA, before reading the Final candidate job.

adversarialFindings.description: The first hosted execution of the staged workflow is the first real test of job wiring, artifact download and shard balance.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Merge only after a green hosted Final candidate on this exact payload. A failure there is fixed at its cause, not retried blindly.

adversarialFindings.description: Each stage repeats checkout, setup, npm ci and, for shards, the Chromium install: more Actions minutes per run.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Accepted by the owner on 2026-11-15 in exchange for shorter waits.

adversarialFindings.description: Changing the workflow and the contract version makes the master merge run FULL, not ATTEST.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Expected for a release-control change; the master FULL run is also the first staged master certification.

retrospective.summary: Proceed to the first hosted run of the staged gate on this payload. The trust model is unchanged: candidate code still certifies itself on GitHub runners, and Final candidate now additionally proves every stage belonged to the same attempt and build. Merge, master FULL and deployment remain separate observations.
